narrative.northStar: The Rhodonite Specimen, put to work
narrative.overview:
The tools are cut from the same stone as itrium.id. That site is The Rhodonite Specimen (`DESIGN.md` in the `website` repository): a graphite matrix with a pink vein, where gray is the body and pink marks what a visitor should find. Here the specimen leaves the display case and goes onto the workbench. The world is the same: Plus Jakarta Sans for everything, graphite and paper, pastel pink with its two deepenings, flat tonal surfaces, pills and soft corners, one drawn arrow. Only the job changes. itrium.id persuades; a tool gets out of the way.

The index is Two halves: the two tools, split edge to edge, one half of the screen each. No metaphor, no cards, no rounded boxes: the halves are the page. Two full-bleed fields with square edges meet on one vertical seam. Split bill's half is always the inverse of the page (graphite on a light page, paper elevated on a dark one), and WhatsApp click-to-chat's half is a tonal step off the page, so the seam reads strongly in both themes. Each half carries its tool's symbol, its name at poster scale, what it does, what leaves it, and one large pink start. Flint's name and its line sit above the halves, a step below the tools' names, and what never leaves sits on the page below them. It replaced the Rantang (#73), which replaced the Device Map (#71), which replaced the line-item strip (#70).

A tool page follows the index. It opens with the tool's title, said as its half says it: the tool's symbol and its name in the same extra-bold type, the introduction under it. Both tools are now drawn in this world (the owner's rounds of 2026-11-24), with no cards. Split bill's parts are divided by plain lines under extra-bold headings, items as rows between lines, and below 1024px the bill is made in three steps, one on screen at a time, with a graphite bar fixed to the bottom of the screen holding the step's count or total and the way on. The person using it is at a restaurant table with a phone in one hand and a group waiting, so they do one job at a time and the answer is one tap away. WhatsApp click-to-chat is the fields, then under a plain line the answer shown as what it becomes: the QR code as it will print, in the open beside "Your link", with "Open in WhatsApp" and "Copy link" under it. From 1024px each tool's answer has its own column.

Components are soft and sure-footed, and tactile without being playful. Every control has a round, generous target that a thumb finds the first time (2.75rem on touch screens) and an edge you can see (3:1 against every surface they sit on). They feel good to press but never perform. Density on the index is bold and wide; inside a tool it is calm and working: below 1024px forms sit in a narrow column of 36 to 42rem, from 1024px a tool takes the 72rem column with its answer beside the form, and the few things that really are boxes (receipt lines, the adjustments list, a note) sit one step back with a hairline round them.

Light and dark are equal. Each follows the visitor's system unless the footer says otherwise, and neither is a courtesy version of the other: every new pairing is designed and checked in both. The system refuses what itrium.id refuses: generic SaaS ornament (gradient text, icon-card rows, invented numbers), drop shadows on anything but a floating list, pure black and white, decorative pink, and small labels above headings. It refuses what only a tool can get wrong: a hero that pushes the tool off a phone screen, and state shown by color alone. And on the index it refuses what the owner has turned down four times over: anything that reads as a receipt (dashed lines, gray-on-paper monochrome, a narrow column, rows of entries), any metaphor (a map, a food carrier), and a column of stacked rounded boxes. On Split bill the owner turned down the same stack: "too many boxes".
keyCharacteristics: One stone with itrium.id: the same tokens, typeface, radii, button shapes and arrow.
The index is two full-bleed halves, square-edged, meeting on one vertical seam from 768 px, their content lined up with the header's 72rem column.
Split bill's half is the inverse of the page in both themes; WhatsApp's half is a tonal step off the page.
The tools' names lead the page at every width, a step above Flint's own name.
Each tool has one fixed symbol, drawn in the text color, the same in the header and in its half.
Pink only at the two starts on the index (equal starts), and at one primary action per tool view.
A tool page opens with its title: the tool's symbol and its name in extra-bold type, as in its half, and the introduction under it.
Split bill has no cards: parts between plain lines, items as rows, three steps below 1024px with a graphite bar at the bottom, and two columns from 1024px.
WhatsApp click-to-chat has no card: the fields, a plain line, then the answer shown as the print it makes, in its own column beside a vertical line from 1024px.
Light and dark are equal. Both follow the system, unless System, Light or Dark is chosen in the footer.
Flat surfaces with tonal steps. The only shadow is under the open searchable list.
Every control has a 3:1 edge (`--control-border`), a target at least 2.75rem tall on touch screens, and 16px text on touch screens so iOS doesn't zoom.
Motion is CSS only and off under reduced motion.

rules.name: The Vein Rule
rules.body: Pink marks something: the primary action, focus, what's selected, or the way onward. If you can't say what a pink element marks, it should be gray. Pink means one thing at a time, which is not the same as one element. In a tool, one pink button per view. On the index, one pink start in each tool's half, the two tools' equal starts ("Split a bill", "Chat with a number"): one meaning, two pills. Rose-text action lines serve the tools elsewhere and a shared bill as their way onward, and nothing else is pink. The seam, the fields, the tool symbols, a tool's title, the step bar and the print are never pink. On Split bill below 1024px the bar's "Next" counts toward the view: it is outlined until the step's own work has started (nobody added on step 1, nothing on the bill on step 2), so the step's own pink action ("Scan or paste a receipt") isn't doubled.

rules.name: The Inverse Field Rule
rules.body: Split bill's half (the `.inverse-field` scope) takes the colors of the theme the page is not in, every one of them: on a light page graphite, with off-white text, muted gray on dark, pink focus, pink edges and pink text, and the dark control edge; on a dark page paper elevated, with graphite text, muted gray on light, deep-rose edges, rose text, graphite focus, and the light control edge. Nothing inside it reads the page's own colors. The owner chose this on 2026-11-24 and accepted its cost: a bright band across a dark page, in exchange for a seam that reads strongly in both themes. The contrast for each pairing is in the comment above the scope in `src/app.css`.

rules.name: The Graphite Bar Rule
rules.body: Split bill's bar at the bottom of a phone's screen is graphite on a light page, with every color inside it from dark mode (the `.graphite-bar` scope: off-white text, pink focus and edges, the dark control edge), like Split bill's half. On a dark page it does not invert: it stays dark, a step up to graphite surface, because a bright band held under the thumb at a dim table is too much.

rules.name: The Two Borders Rule
rules.body: `--border` is for lines nothing depends on, such as dividing lines and the edges of inset lists and the print. Anything a person has to find in order to use it gets `--control-border`.

rules.name: The Graphite Text Rule
rules.body: Text on pink is graphite, never white. On light backgrounds pink text is rose text and pink lines are deep rose. Pastel pink is never text or a line there.

rules.name: The Every-Surface Rule
rules.body: Contrast is checked on every surface text sits on: page, inset list, note, the print, the bottom bar, update notice, the error page's panel, and each half in both themes. Text needs 4.5:1. Focus outlines, control edges and state lines need 3:1. The tightest are Split bill's half on a light page (control edge 3.7:1) and on a dark page (muted 4.7:1, rose text 4.8:1).

rules.name: The One Typeface Rule
rules.body: Plus Jakarta Sans does everything. Never add a second family, and never load a font from another domain.

rules.name: The Tools Lead Rule
rules.body: On the index, the tools' names are the largest type at every width, and Flint's own name steps down with them: 40 over 36 on phones, 60 over 48 from 640 px, 48 over 36 from 768 px, 64 over 48 from 1024 px, 72 over 60 from 1280 px. A new size for one is a new size for the other. On a tool page the tool's title is the largest type, in the same extra-bold voice.

rules.name: The No Kicker Rule
rules.body: A heading is the first thing in its block. No eyebrow, category label, small uppercase heading or back link sits above it. Nothing here is set in uppercase. A line that says more about a heading goes under it or beside it, as Flint's line does. A half's symbol sits above the tool's name, but it is the tool's picture, not a label.

rules.name: The Two Halves Rule
rules.body: The index is the tools, one full-bleed field each, side by side from 768 px and meeting on one seam. A field holds its tool's symbol, name, what it does, what leaves it and its own pink start, and nothing else. No cards inside or around them, no hero over them, no column of boxes.

rules.name: The Kept Space Rule
rules.body: What the browser remembers arrives into a space already kept for it (what a tool does keeps two lines, 2.75em; the shared bill's line keeps 3rem, `kept-line`, in both halves), so nothing moves under a finger when it appears. The same holds inside a tool: the empty print keeps its place, the line under the number keeps two lines, "Copy link" keeps its width when it says "Copied", and what the code holds is said in one line that swaps its words when the box is ticked.

rules.name: The Slab Rule, for tools
rules.body: A tool page has no slab at either end: it opens with the tool's title, its symbol and its name, and never closes with a panel. On a phone, the tool comes before the frame.

rules.name: The One Job Rule
rules.body: Below 1024px Split bill shows one step at a time, and the steps are free: any tab, in any order. Whatever a control sends focus to brings its own step on screen first (`focusAfter`), so "Show it" from the split lands on the item in step 2. A step is a view, not a gate: nothing is removed from the page, and nothing is checked before moving on.

rules.name: The First Screen Rule
rules.body: On a phone, the first field of a tool is visible without scrolling, and on the index Split bill's start is. If a new element would push either down, it belongs lower on the page.

rules.name: The Answer In Reach Rule
rules.body: Wherever a tool is being filled in, its answer is one glance or one tap away: the step bar and the bottom bar's total below 1024 px, the split's own column above; on WhatsApp click-to-chat, the line reading the number back under its field, and the answer right under the fields, nothing floating over it. Someone opening a shared result lands on it, not on the form that made it.

rules.name: The Only Floating Things Cast Shadows Rule
rules.body: Halves, buttons, chips, the error page's panel, the print and the bottom bar never get a drop shadow. A control responds by filling with the next tonal step, a header link by its underline, and an arrow by moving 4 px on.

rules.name: The Square Seam Rule
rules.body: The halves have square edges and meet on one straight line. No arcs, rails, rims, dashes or shadows on the index.

rules.name: The Pinned Fact Rule
rules.body: What leaves a tool is said in that tool's half, above its start, before anyone presses it. What never leaves is said once, under the halves. Never collect them into a legend or a list apart from the tools they concern.

rules.name: The Peer Rule
rules.body: The two halves are equal: the same type, the same rhythm, the same size of start. Neither tool is a hero over the other; the inverse field gives Split bill the stronger tone only so the seam shows, not to rank it.

rules.name: The Whole Edge Rule
rules.body: A note is marked by its whole edge, never by a thick bar down one side.

dos: **Do** take tokens, radii, button shapes, the arrow and type roles from itrium.id's DESIGN.md before inventing anything. A difference between the two sites needs a reason a tool has and a page doesn't.

**Do** add to the index as a half: a new tool is a new full-bleed field with square edges, its symbol, its name, what it does, what leaves it, and its own pink start, its content on the header's 72rem column.
**Do** keep Split bill's half the inverse of the page in both themes, with every color inside it from the other theme (`.inverse-field`), and check each pairing in it when one is added.
**Do** keep the tools' names a step above Flint's at every width, and each name two lines tall side by side, so the rows meet across the seam.
**Do** give every tool one symbol and use it wherever the tool is named in the frame: the header and its half.
**Do** keep a tool's first field, and Split bill's start on the index, on the first phone screen, and both starts on the first screen at 1280 by 800 and 1440 by 900.
**Do** give every field, button and chip a `--control-border` edge and a touch target at least 2.75rem tall on touch screens.

**Do** show every state in two ways: a check mark with the pink fill, words with the pink edge, an underline on the current page's link, and the reason a button can't be pressed yet, said under it when someone presses or reaches it (not at rest, and not read out again after every add).
**Do** design and check every new pairing in light and dark, on every surface it sits on.
**Do** use the drawn arrow wherever a link points onward.

**Do** keep motion in CSS, gated on `motion-safe` or `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference`: page cross-fades, the theme cross-fade (a view transition, when someone picks a theme or the device switches under System), the 4 px arrow nudge, and the loading spinner. Nothing rises or reveals as it scrolls.
**Do** open a tool page with its title: its symbol, its name in extra-bold tool-title type, and the introduction under it, lined up with the header and the tool.
**Do** divide a tool's parts with plain hairlines under extra-bold part headings, and set items as rows between lines; keep a box only for a list checked line by line or a note asking for attention.
**Do** keep every step of Split bill in the page, shown or hidden by its step, and bring a step on screen before focusing anything in it.
**Do** count the bottom bar's "Next" in a view's one pink action: outlined until the step's own work has started.
**Do** use Tailwind classes with the theme tokens and the shared classes in `src/lib/styles.ts`, never raw hex values in markup.
donts: **Don't** make the index read as a receipt, on any cue: no dashed lines, no gray-on-paper monochrome, no narrow column, no rows of entries. The owner turned down the line-item strip (#70) and the Device Map (#71) for exactly this.
**Don't** give the index a metaphor: no map, no food carrier, no object for the tools to sit in. The owner turned down the Device Map (#71) and the Rantang (#73) for this.
**Don't** draw the index as a column of stacked rounded boxes, or put cards, a legend or a hero over the halves.
**Don't** round the halves, inset them from the screen's edges, or draw an arc, rail, rim, dash or shadow on the index.

**Don't** use pink as decoration, or give pink two meanings in one view: a tool has one pink button, and the index's two starts are both the primary action, one in each half. The seam, the fields and the symbols are never pink.

**Don't** add a structural gray outside the palette. Its one exception, the error panel's raised border in dark mode (#4f4f4f), is a structural step above a palette gray; a new one needs the same reason, and a color change otherwise belongs in `@itrium/palettes`.
**Don't** put a small uppercase heading, eyebrow, kicker or back link above a heading.
**Don't** type arrows or chevrons as characters.
**Don't** give halves, buttons, chips, the print, the error panel or the bottom bar a drop shadow.
**Don't** put Split bill's parts back in cards, or stack rounded boxes in a tool: the owner turned that down as "too many boxes".
